items.item_text: Graduate of radiology technology training program approved by the American Medical Association or equivalent training.
18 months of experience in radiologic technology; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Ensure compliance with applicable safety and regulator standards, service needs of SHS and its patients, and standards established by the Chief Physician. Perform radiological studies adhering to accepted technical and safety standards, e.g. proper positioning of the patient. Select proper technical factors and program equipment accordingly to produce optimal radiographic image and ensure quality control standards. Develop film using standardized processing methods. Provide radiation safety protection in accordance with prescribed safety standards. Ensure orderliness and cleanliness of all areas to optimize care services. Direct patient flow to ensure prompt provision of services. Monitor and ensure appropriate and accurate use of automated systems used by the unit. Participate in assessing film selection and other technical factors to attain optimal results. Introduce new imaging technologies and product innovation as directed, and in cooperation with Chief Physician, Providers, and staff. (80% time)

Ensure practice of customer service and continuous quality improvement philosophies. Train new per-diem staff before they are able to cover for sick and vacation as well as ongoing training when new systems are utilized. Review work of per-diem staff for peer review purposes. Provide and review statistics on utilization with input from the business operations manager. Support ongoing coverage for unit operations. Using judgment and discretion, problem solve, resolve issues related to SHS Radiology. Maintain ongoing awareness of industry standards. Maintain all safety standards and regulations, as needed to pass inspection from the California Department of Public Health and The Acreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC). Arrange for transportation of patients as needed. (20% time)
Licensure by State of California, Department of Health Services, as Certified Radiologic Technologist.
Registered for membership in American Registry of Radiologic Technologists.

Skill in operating radiographic film processor.
Demonstrated experience working in a college or university environment.
Ability to assess radiographic film quality.
Skill in using the standard fixed and mobile x-ray imaging equipment.
Ability to work as part of a team, and ability to establish cooperativeworking relationships with administrators, supervisors, doctors, peers and public.
Oral and written communication skills to collect and clearly conveyinformation to physicians, staff, patients and the public, using correct vocabulary, grammar and tact.
